headline: No documented interaction pathway; both open-source agents show no network egress and no shared surfaces, so pairwise risks are limited by missing evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between langchain4j and risingwave, and both profiles show empty io_surfaces plus network_egress:none. Without a bridge, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path between them.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future clipboard or file-based handoff between them.
Add provenance tags to any exchanged text.
requires-engineering: enforce input sanitization on any shared bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show shared storage, shared OAuth, or data classes touched, and both agents report network_egress:none. With no documented data path, leakage from langchain4j to risingwave or vice versa is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared workspace is introduced and either agent uploads file contents, leakage risk increases.
IF sensitive data classes are later assigned to either agent, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared directory.
Keep sensitive inputs out of both agents.
Review any future OAuth scopes before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add access controls and audit logging.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, databases, git state, or network write capabilities are documented for either langchain4j or risingwave. With empty io_surfaces and network_egress:none on both sides, a write-write conflict is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free mutable state, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same resource.
Separate any future databases or git repos.
Use a single writer pattern if shared state is unavoidable.
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented pipeline where risingwave consumes langchain4j outputs as authoritative input, and neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority. Without a verified handoff, cascading error is not evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF risingwave is configured to act on langchain4j outputs without verification, reassess.
IF a downstream automation step is added after langchain4j, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action.
Require schema validation on exchanged outputs.
Keep the agents in separate stages unless a verifier is added.
requires-engineering: add confidence checks and rollback handling.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source with no touched data classes listed. The evidence does not support a compliance mismatch between langchain4j and risingwave.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is later routed through either agent, reassess compliance.
IF one agent is deployed under a stricter residency policy than the other, reassess.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent.
Avoid sending regulated data until policies are confirmed.
Document retention settings for both systems.
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls.
